stem: A client has recurrent torsades de pointes associated with a prolonged QT interval. Which statement about IV magnesium is accurate?

options.A: Routine magnesium is recommended for every episode of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, including episodes with a normal QT interval.
options.B: Magnesium replaces immediate unsynchronized shock when sustained polymorphic ventricular tachycardia is present.
options.C: Magnesium may be considered to suppress recurrences of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes).
options.D: Magnesium is contraindicated in torsades de pointes because it predictably worsens QT-related ventricular instability.

rationale: The 2025 AHA Adult Advanced Life Support guideline states that immediate unsynchronized shock is recommended for sustained polymorphic VT. For recurrences associated with a long QT interval (torsades de pointes), magnesium may be considered. Routine magnesium is not recommended for polymorphic VT with a normal QT interval. Therefore C is correct; A overgeneralizes magnesium use, B incorrectly substitutes medication for required defibrillation of sustained polymorphic VT, and D reverses the guideline recommendation.
educational_objective: Differentiate treatment of long-QT torsades from other polymorphic ventricular tachycardia: defibrillate sustained polymorphic VT promptly and consider magnesium for recurrent torsades associated with long QT.

options.B: Magnesium replaces immediate unsynchronized shock when sustained polymorphic VT is unstable

source_original.rationale: Current AHA adult advanced life support guidance recommends immediate unsynchronized shock for sustained polymorphic VT. Magnesium may be considered for recurrences of polymorphic VT associated with long QT (torsades), but routine magnesium is not recommended when the QT is normal.
source_original.source_detail: Polymorphic ventricular tachycardia section: shock for sustained polymorphic VT; magnesium may be considered for recurrent torsades with long QT; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Retained the correct long-QT torsades distinction, tied every alternative directly to the 2025 AHA polymorphic-VT recommendations, and reduced editorial difficulty from hard to medium because the final construct is a focused guideline application.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Torsades de pointes / polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
audit_findings.source_authority: AHA 2025 Adult Advanced Life Support; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.currentness: 2025 AHA CPR/ECC guideline is the current cited ALS source.
audit_findings.claim_audit: AHA Section 16 directly supports immediate shock for sustained polymorphic VT, consideration of magnesium for recurrent long-QT torsades, and no routine magnesium for normal-QT polymorphic VT.

distractor_audit.B: False by AHA Recommendation 1; medication must not replace prompt defibrillation of sustained polymorphic VT.
distractor_audit.D: False; magnesium is specifically a treatment option for recurrent torsades.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: C is the only statement matching the long-QT recurrent-torsades recommendation without contradicting shock priority.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address magnesium's role in the same rhythm-management construct.
audit_findings.blueprint: NCSBN p.12 Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read AHA Section 16, challenged the distinction between recurrent torsades and sustained polymorphic VT, re-evaluated all four choices, and confirmed NCSBN p.12 mapping. C remained uniquely correct.
